title: Injector: shortcut tooltip on the panel title, and triggers message only the terminal that got full
story: The Injector's Triggers no longer ask who should get the message. A trigger now always messages only the terminal whose context passed the percent; the old 'every terminal it watches' option is gone, and triggers saved with it now act the same way. Rows read 'At N% context', and the last-fired line says delivered or failed instead of a count. Hovering the Injector panel title now shows its Alt+4 shortcut.

checks.criterion: Hovering the Injector panel title shows 'Injector (Alt+4)'
checks.steps: Start Maestro, press Alt+4 to open the Injector, hover the word 'Injector' in the panel header.
checks.expected: A tooltip reading 'Injector (Alt+4)' (on a Mac, the Option-key form).

checks.criterion: The trigger form has no 'send the message to' choice
checks.steps: Open the Injector, scroll to Triggers, look at the add form, then click the pencil on any trigger.
checks.expected: Both forms read 'When a terminal reaches [80]% context, it gets:' with no drop-down after it. Rows read 'At 80% context'.

checks.criterion: A trigger sends its message only to the watched terminal that passed the percent
checks.steps: Open three Claude terminals (alpha, beta, gamma), tick all three in the Injector, add a trigger watching the ticked ones at 5% with the message 'hello test'. Work in beta until its context passes 5%.
checks.expected: Only beta receives 'hello test' and gets the envelope icon. The row says 'Last fired HH:MM by beta: delivered', and History lists 'sent to beta'.

checks.criterion: A saved trigger with target 'all' loads and behaves as 'only that terminal'
checks.steps: Quit Maestro. In the app data injector-triggers.json set a trigger to {"id":"old","name":"Old","watch":"all","threshold":5,"message":"hello old","target":"all"}. Start Maestro, open two terminals, push one past 5%.
checks.expected: The trigger 'Old' is listed with no send-to text, and only the terminal that passed 5% gets 'hello old'.
